desc:
The array nums has even length n and contains exactly n / 2 even numbers (so the other n / 2 are odd). In one move you may swap any two elements.

Return the minimum number of moves after which every even index holds an even number and every odd index holds an odd number.

nums = [4, 2, 5, 7]
result = 1

Here 2 sits at index 1 and 5 sits at index 2; swapping them fixes both.
hints: Call a position wrong if its parity does not match its index. Which wrong positions can a single swap repair?
A swap repairs two positions at once when it exchanges an odd value standing at an even index with an even value standing at an odd index.

Because exactly half of the values are even, the number of odd values at even indices always equals the number of even values at odd indices. The answer is that common number, so one counting pass is enough.
editorial: Split the wrong positions in two groups: odd values sitting at even indices (call this count a) and even values sitting at odd indices (count b). The array has n / 2 even indices and n / 2 even values. The even indices are filled by n / 2 - a even values, so n / 2 - (n / 2 - a) = a even values live at odd indices, hence a = b.
A swap can fix at most two wrong positions, and swapping one wrong item of each group fixes exactly two. So a swaps are necessary and sufficient.
Counting takes one pass: O(n) time and O(1) space. Careful with negative numbers: use x % 2 (or x & 1), not a comparison with 1 after a remainder operator that keeps the sign.
